video.title: 4 Tips For Consistently Crushing Slow Balls

classification.reason: The coach explains four principles for attacking slow balls on the forehand with an on-court demonstrator and targeted drills.

problem.title_as_question: How can you consistently attack and crush slow balls?
problem.definition: Slow, floating balls lack front-to-back penetration, making them very difficult to attack unless the player generates penetration through body weight, proper prep height, early positioning, and precise tracking.
prerequisites: able to track and hit standard groundstrokes

quotes.text: Slow balls are not easy. These shots are actually very high degree of difficulty shots.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: They're easy to see and to track, but they are not easy to attack.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The slow ball, it's not penetrating through this way. It's just coming straight down. So all of that frontto back penetration action has to be created by the player hitting the ball.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Now you'll notice it's landing in front of where it starts. We call this positive balance or at least that's what I like to call it. Balance. That means that your weight ends in front of where it started.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Now, I want you to try and attack these while staying in place. So, try to not go forward and attack these.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So, you'll notice she doesn't even really look like a pro player anymore because that positive balance is so ingrained into the proper way to attack these balls
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We're going to take the band and we're going to put it around our waist. This is going to add resistance in that vector that we want to push along.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And you could just drop feed yourself these balls. And now you have to press against the resistance of the band while the band is resisting you.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: you're going to get that feeling in the back leg, that power of your legs through the court that penetrates the ball, which you need to attack slow balls using this.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If you prepare way below the ball, the only thing you can successfully do is moonball it back.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If you watch Alex's hand here, that hand is almost always level with the ball. There is only a very slight low to high diagonal.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: look at the ball's height and think about preparing your hand at the ball's height so you can hit it flatter and not try to hit that spin which is never going to work on this kind of a ball
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So, that last ball Alexa hit, she hit it here when it was about 2, three feet above the height of the net still, even though she started behind the baseline.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Remember how in the last section we said you want to prepare your hand at the height of the ball and hit that ball flat? Well, guess what? You can't do that unless the ball is above the net.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Realistically speaking, if you don't react to this ball on time and you end up getting it low, you should really just chip it and run back to the baseline. You cannot attack the ball from your knees
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The final and most critical piece is you need to watch the ball. And you have to watch the ball hit the ground.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Now, your brain doesn't feel like that ball is threatening. It feels like, oh, it's so slow, like I barely even have to look at it. I know where it is. I promise you, you don't know where it is.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: When you watch it hit the ground, you're going to see it come off the ground clearly, and you're actually going to be able to do all this with intention.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: They run up to the ball. They have no idea where it is. They do all these things, but they take a random swing through kind of a random point in the air.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So remember while you're doing this that the ultimate goal is to strike the ball in space.
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: The incoming slow ball lacks court penetration and drops downward rather than travelling toward the player.
The player hits weak moonballs or misses inconsistently when trying to drive the ball.
The player takes a random swing through an arbitrary point in the air instead of coordinating contact with the actual ball.

causes.statement: Slow floating balls lack incoming front-to-back momentum, requiring the hitter to actively produce court penetration that a fast ball normally provides.
The player attacks while staying stationary instead of establishing positive balance where the back foot and body weight land forward.
The player prepares the hitting hand way below the height of the ball, forcing excessive topspin or an upward moonball trajectory instead of driving through flatter.
The player fails to recognize the short floater early and sprint up to contact it above net height, letting the ball drop down to knee level.
Because the ball looks non-threatening, the player assumes they know where it is and fails to track it all the way down to the bounce.

angles.summary: Because a floater drops vertically without penetrating forward, the player's back foot and weight must drive forward across contact to create depth.
Demonstrator tries to attack a slow ball while staying completely in place, illustrating that without forward weight drive the strike looks awkward and unathletic.
Players wrongly drop the racket head far below slow balls trying to generate excessive topspin, which makes driving floating balls wildly inconsistent.
A resistance band around the waist gives the hitter a direct sensory feeling of driving the back leg and body weight through the court vector.
The brain treats non-threatening slow balls casually; watching the ball bounce off the ground provides the visual precision needed to coordinate the swing in space.

solutions.summary: Attach a resistance band around the waist (anchored behind by a partner or fence) and hit self-dropped balls while driving forward against the band tension to feel back-leg push.
solutions.external_goal: Press against the resistance band while driving the back foot forward past its start point.

solutions.summary: Look at the height of the ball and prepare your hand at ball height to drive through on a very slight low-to-high trajectory rather than dropping way beneath it.
solutions.external_goal: Prepare the hand level with the incoming ball's height.

solutions.summary: Recognize the short ball early and sprint forward to catch it 2 to 3 feet above net level before it drops below net height.
solutions.external_goal: Make contact with the ball 2 to 3 feet above net height.

solutions.summary: Lock your eyes onto the ball and deliberately watch it hit the ground so you can track it cleanly off the bounce into contact.
solutions.external_goal: Watch the ball make contact with the court surface.
